records.title: Natural Numbers
records.definition: Whole numbers used for counting, with convention-dependent inclusion of zero.
principles: Natural numbers can be ordered and counted.
relationships: Natural numbers are part of the integers.
misconceptions: Natural numbers are not the same as all real numbers.
assessment_ideas: Identify natural numbers from a list.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Integers
records.definition: Positive and negative whole numbers together with zero.
principles: Adding or subtracting integers produces another integer.
relationships: Integers contain the natural numbers and form part of the rational numbers.
misconceptions: A negative number can still have a large absolute value.
assessment_ideas: Place integers correctly on a number line.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Rational Numbers
records.definition: Numbers that can be expressed as a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.
principles: The denominator of a rational-number fraction cannot be zero.
relationships: Integers are rational numbers; rational numbers are real numbers.
misconceptions: Not every decimal number is rational.
assessment_ideas: Classify numbers as rational or not rational.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Variables
records.definition: A symbol representing a quantity whose value may be unknown or may change.
principles: An expression can be evaluated after assigning a value to its variable.
relationships: Variables occur in expressions, equations, functions and models.
misconceptions: A variable does not always represent an unknown.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard algebraic definitions

records.title: Equations
records.definition: A mathematical statement that two expressions have equal values.
principles: Applying the same valid operation to both sides preserves equality.
relationships: Equations use variables and can represent mathematical models.
misconceptions: An equation is not simply an expression.
assessment_ideas: Solve and verify a linear equation.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard algebraic definitions
